method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, forward reconstruction of the meta-level modus-ponens result, both directions of the Deduction Theorem, the induction basis and step, and all five exercise claims; exact structural comparison was performed after the documented OLAXD-001 source projection. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The proof-theoretic Deduction Theorem for axiomatic derivations, its induction proof, a meta-level modus-ponens lemma, and five derivability exercises.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Reflexivity, monotonicity and transitivity let us reason about derivations without displaying every line. If Gamma derives A and A-implies-B, the explicit three-line derivation from those two hypotheses plus transitivity gives Gamma derives B.
samples.checks: All three cited structural properties, their premise-set directions, the meta-level modus-ponens proposition and the three derivation lines remain exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The Deduction Theorem states that Gamma together with A derives B exactly when Gamma derives A-implies-B. The forward use in the source's if direction follows by monotonicity, reflexivity and the preceding meta-level modus-ponens proposition.
samples.checks: Both sides of the biconditional, the union with singleton A, all intermediate sequents and all three references preserve their direction.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: For the only-if direction, induct on derivation length. At length one, B is either in Gamma union {A} or is an axiom. If B belongs to Gamma or is an axiom, ax:lif1 and meta-MP yield A-implies-B; if B equals A, use the previously derived identity A-implies-A.
samples.checks: The length-one split, membership alternatives, ax:lif1 instance, identity reference, and every occurrence of A and B are preserved.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: If the last B-line follows by modus ponens from earlier C-implies-B and C lines, their shorter derivations satisfy the induction hypothesis, giving A-implies-(C-implies-B) and A-implies-C. Ax:lif2 followed by meta-MP twice yields A-implies-B.
samples.checks: The non-MP fallback cases, both shorter derivability statements, both induction-hypothesis conclusions, the ax:lif2 formula and two meta-MP applications are exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The conditional axioms were selected to support the Deduction Theorem. Exercises ask for a conditional-composition theorem, contraposition, explosion, double-negation elimination and its Gamma-level consequence, with separate first-order and propositional problem links.
samples.checks: All five claims, five item labels, two protected problem tags and two four-part references are preserved. OLAXD-001 adds only the missing outer right parenthesis to the first formula.

source_observations: OLAXD-001 documents a deterministically missing outer right parenthesis in the first derivability exercise. The Marathi target supplies one parenthesis and carries an adjacent stable reader note; frozen English bytes remain unchanged.
The source names the first theorem implication as the if direction because its assumed side is Gamma derives A-implies-B; the Marathi preserves that orientation.
The induction is on the length of a concrete derivation of B from Gamma union {A}, with the only nontrivial final-line case supplied by modus ponens.
All formulas, macros, tokens, labels, identifiers and reference options match after the documented OLAXD-001 projection.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
निगमन प्रमेय, the transparent explosion gloss and the compositional double-negation-elimination name remain open to expert review under T186, T188 and T189.
The five final derivability facts are intentionally left without proofs in the source.
